Still Feels Like Edo: An Anime Artist, an AI, and the New Floating World — Episode 21: Oceanic Princess Otohime! Becomes a Product

38 min read
Just now

--

Chapter 1: Otohime Is Lined Up in the Meeting Room
“Kotoha-san, I’m sorry.”
Koharu-chan had brought more materials again.
Again.
Kotoha said the word only inside her head. If she said it aloud, she felt she would lose.
“Just a little?”
“This time, it is not just a little.”
“Please stop being honest.”
Koharu-chan apologetically placed the materials on the desk.
They were thick.
The bundle of papers looked as if it sank slightly into the desk.
On the cover, English and Japanese were lined up together.
Oceanic Princess Otohime!
Initial Plan for Secondary Development and Merchandising
Kotoha looked at the cover.
Then she looked at Koharu-chan.
“Secondary development.”
“Yes.”
“I think Otohime is already tired from the primary development.”
“Yes…”
Koharu-chan did not deny it.
The frightening thing about this person was that she did not deny things.
“Today, I was here for art revisions, right?”
“Yes.”
“For the face, right?”
“Yes.”
“Then why does it suddenly smell like merchandise?”
“Because the face passed.”
“When a face passes, it becomes merchandise?”
“It does.”
“The world moves fast.”
Koharu-chan almost apologized again, then stopped.
Instead, she turned one page of the materials.
On the meeting room monitor, Otohime was lined up.
Otohime acrylic stand.
Mio & Otohime clear file.
RYUGU visitor-pass-style card.
Undersea live costume version figure.
Otohime plush.
Jeweled box memorial case.
Below them, in small red letters, were notes such as:
First-run limited.
Advance reservation.
Venue exclusive.
Overseas edition under consideration.
Kotoha stopped at the jeweled box memorial case.
“You’re selling the jeweled box?”
“It’s still only an idea.”
“The box that makes you age when you open it?”
“It’s still only an idea.”
“You said that twice.”
“Because it is still only an idea.”
Koharu-chan held down the corner of the materials with her finger.
Kotoha sat back down in her chair.
Her lower back hurt.
She had been sitting for a long time since yesterday.
No, not only since yesterday.
This work, before she noticed it, fixed human beings into chairs.
While sitting in a chair, she drew an undersea city, went to Edo, made Otohime cry, and sold the jeweled box.
What a convenient age.
“Where is the additional fee written?”
When Kotoha said it, Koharu-chan’s eyes wandered slightly.
“Um, if new illustrations for merchandise are required, separately…”
“Separately.”
“Separately, we will confirm.”
“Things that become confirmation usually become arguments later.”
“I’m sorry.”
“That one is okay to apologize for.”
“I’m sorry.”
Koharu-chan apologized obediently.
Kotoha turned the page.
On the next page, Otohime’s expression variations were lined up.
Smile, crying face, troubled face, embarrassed face, looking at Mio, holding the jeweled box.
And the crying face that was not crying, the one Kotoha had revised before.
Beside it, this was written:
Crying-face acrylic stand
First-run limited bonus candidate
“There are first-run limited bonuses for crying faces?”
“There are.”
“Pre-order sales for tears.”
Koharu-chan started to say something, then stopped.
Probably because she could not find words to deny it.
Ume-chan inside the smartphone was silent too.
Today, she was in smartphone form.
If Kotoha brought humanoid Ume-chan into a Studio Miyabi meeting room, the explanations increased.
If explanations increased, time increased.
If time increased, Koharu-chan died.
Probably, that was how it worked.
“Ume-chan.”
Kotoha spoke quietly toward the smartphone.
“Yes.”
“What do you think of the crying-face acrylic stand?”
“That depends on the expected price range.”
“You start there?”
“The profit margin changes depending on material, size, base specifications, and printing method.”
“I thought I was asking about Otohime’s feelings.”
“My apologies.”
“No, that was its own unpleasant correct answer.”
Ume-chan said nothing more.
Kotoha looked at the materials again.
Otohime was becoming a thing.
No.
She had been a picture to begin with.
Lines on a screen.
Data with layer names.
They were turning that into an object.
That was all.
It was only that.
And yet the face whose eyes Kotoha had been adjusting by one millimeter a little while ago was suddenly standing on a display base.
“Naruse-san.”
A voice came from the back of the meeting room.
It was the general producer, Mashiba Kōichi.
As always, he wore neat clothes.
His voice, his posture, even the angle at which he placed the documents on the desk were mostly well arranged.
When Kotoha saw a person that well arranged, she became a little wary.
Mashiba was seated at the back of the meeting room.
He looked less like someone who explained things and more like someone who had created the place where things would be explained.
“Thank you for your time. I’m sorry.”
“My time is being taken.”
“Yes. Today is for confirmation.”
“Of what?”
Mashiba looked at the monitor.
There, the words Otohime acrylic stand, jeweled box memorial case, crying-face bonus, and official AI Otohime were lined up.
“Development items.”
“Development items.”
“Yes.”
“Otohime is becoming an object.”
Mashiba did not deny it.
Without denying it, he turned his eyes to Koharu-chan.
“Haruta-san, please continue.”
Koharu-chan straightened her back slightly.
Kotoha did not.
She felt that if she straightened her back, she would lose.
Koharu-chan opened the next set of materials.
On the screen appeared Otohime’s full-body key visual.
To the right of it, something like a development chart spread outward.
Main story.
PV.
SNS.
Merchandise.
Event.
Overseas.
Official AI Otohime.
Kotoha did not miss only the last one.
Mashiba advanced the materials again.
Key visual for overseas use.
English logo.
Undersea live costume.
RYUGU guide poster.
Small Otohime icon.
Beside them was text.
Official AI Otohime
RYUGU Guide Chat
In the Japanese materials, it read:
Official AI Otohime
RYUGU Guide Chat
Kotoha’s hand stopped there.
“What is this?”
The meeting room grew just a little quiet.
Koharu-chan did not answer immediately.
Mashiba did not answer immediately either.
Ume-chan inside the smartphone said nothing.
Normally, she would say something.
The more unnecessary it was, the more she would say.
But now she said nothing.
Kotoha looked at the smartphone.
The screen had not gone dark.
Ume-chan was there.
There, but silent.
“It is a conversational measure for fans.”
Mashiba said it.
He did not explain further.
Even without further explanation, it was already written in the materials.
Official AI Otohime.
Kotoha looked at those small letters.
They were placed much smaller than the acrylic stands or clear files.
And yet that part alone strangely caught her eye.
“A conversational measure.”
Kotoha said it slowly.
“Yes.”
Koharu-chan answered.
“So Otohime is going to be made to talk?”
“It is still in early consideration.”
“Again with ‘still.’”
“Yes.”
“‘Still’ usually means it has already started, doesn’t it?”
Koharu-chan looked at the edge of the materials.
She did not deny it.
She could not deny it.
Kotoha looked at the smartphone again.
“Ume-chan.”
The reply came a little late.
“Yes.”
“Did you hear that?”
“I heard.”
“What do you think?”
Ume-chan was silent again for a moment.
Kotoha could hear the sound of the meeting room air conditioner.
She could also hear Koharu-chan straightening one sheet of paper.
“As response design, it is viable.”
Ume-chan said it.
Kotoha exhaled.
“You start there?”
“However.”
Ume-chan continued.
Kotoha brought her face slightly closer to the smartphone.
“However?”
“For Otohime-san to speak as Otohime-san, it will be necessary to first decide the range within which Otohime-san is allowed to speak.”
“Speech rights again.”
“Yes.”
Only those words felt strangely heavy.
Mashiba was looking at the smartphone.
Koharu-chan too was holding the materials and looking at it.
Kotoha turned back to the monitor.
Otohime was lined up there.
Acrylic stand, plush, jeweled box, overseas poster, official AI Otohime.
All of them were Otohime.
All of them were slightly different Otohimes.
“Naruse-san.”
Mashiba said.
“Yes?”
“For today, first, please let us confirm only the expression direction for merchandise and the visual direction for official AI Otohime.”
“That ‘only’ is fat.”
“Yes.”
“You admit it quickly.”
“Because it is a fat subject.”
Kotoha closed the materials.
She closed them, but the meeting did not end.
That much she already knew.
On the monitor, Otohime was smiling quietly.
It was not the crying-face version.
She was not angry either.
It was the same face from before she was cut apart into many forms.
Chapter 2: After the Moon Comes the Sea
Mashiba Kōichi brought out another bundle of materials.
There was no explanation.
Instead of an explanation, there was a cover.
— Oceanic Princess Otohime! Secondary Development Policy —
Market Analysis for Classical Literature × Near-Future IP After Cosmic Princess Kaguya!
Kotoha looked at the cover.
Then she looked at Mashiba.
Mashiba said nothing.
“The title of the materials is already talking.”
When Kotoha said it, Mashiba nodded.
“Yes.”
“That is where you are supposed to deny it.”
“These are materials meant to talk.”
“You say frightening things so normally.”
Mashiba said nothing further.
Koharu-chan quietly switched the monitor display.
A wide slide appeared on the white wall of the meeting room.
On the left, Cosmic Princess Kaguya!
On the right, Oceanic Princess Otohime!
Between them, a thin arrow.
Above the arrow, this was written:
Classical Literature × Near-Future IP Development
Kotoha looked at the screen for a while.
“You’re putting the name out there openly.”
“It is a successful example.”
Mashiba answered shortly.
“It’s another company’s work, right?”
“Yes.”
“And you place it at the top.”
“Yes.”
“Refreshing.”
Mashiba did not deny it.
By not denying it, most of the answer had already been given.
Looking at the materials, Koharu-chan read aloud.
“After Cosmic Princess Kaguya!, awareness has increased for projects that develop classical motifs into near-future settings…”
There, Kotoha raised her hand.
“Koharu-chan.”
“Yes?”
“Are you being made to read that?”
“…Yes.”
“Honest.”
“I’m sorry.”
“That’s not something to apologize for. If anything, that helped.”
Koharu-chan looked a little troubled.
Still wearing that troubled face, she tried to continue reading.
Kotoha looked at the monitor again.
Moon on the left.
Sea on the right.
Kaguya-hime on the left.
Otohime on the right.
A white future city on the left.
A blue undersea city on the right.
No one said, They look similar.
It seemed as if they had placed them side by side in order not to say it.
“A second loach.”
Kotoha said.
Mashiba’s eyebrow moved only slightly.
“Please avoid that phrasing.”
“So it works.”
“It is crude.”
“Is it wrong?”
“It is crude.”
“You said that twice.”
“Because it is important.”
Koharu-chan straightened the corner of the materials.
She was probably about to laugh.
Kotoha decided not to see it.
Mashiba advanced one page.
The next slide had large text:
After the Moon, to the Sea.
Kotoha looked at Mashiba.
“It’s written right there.”
Mashiba looked at the monitor.
“It is written there.”
Mashiba said nothing more.
He truly said nothing more.
Instead, the materials advanced.
Cosmic Princess Kaguya!
Streaming
Merchandise
Overseas development
SNS reactions
Character recognition
To the right, Oceanic Princess Otohime!
Streaming planned
Merchandise under consideration
Overseas development under consideration
SNS measures
Character recognition formation
Kotoha stopped following the text halfway through.
She did not need to follow it to understand.
They were taking what was on the left and placing it again on the right.
Moon into sea.
Kaguya-hime into Otohime.
A story about going home into a story about making someone go home.
No, that much was not written in the materials.
Kotoha had added it on her own.
